title: Flaky: VS Code extension Blazor browser debugger E2E tests fail with websocket proxy launch failure and WASM root session timeouts on Linux
test_name: Aspire Blazor browser debugger E2E hits a managed breakpoint for standalone / hosted-global / hosted-per-page
job_name: Tests / Run VS Code extension E2E tests / VS Code extension E2E (Linux, browser-debugger)
error_pattern: Error: Blazor debugger launch failed: ... "Unable to launch browser: \"Could not open ws://localhost:43999/_framework/debug/ws-proxy?browser=ws%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1...\""; and Error: Timed out after ~299600ms waiting for Blazor WASM root session for resource 'hosted-global'/'hosted-per-page'. Last error: <none>.
analysis: The failure is a timeout waiting for the Blazor WASM managed debugger to attach a root session during the VS Code extension's E2E test harness. This is an environment/timing issue in the debugger-launch pipeline (websocket proxy connectivity, browser launch race), not something explainable by the PR's changes, which are confined to Aspire.Hosting DCP/executable/container-network provisioning code with no touches to the VS Code extension or its debugger E2E infrastructure. Matches a previously tracked recurring flaky cause (issue #20184).
